item.title: OnStep CG5 Conversion
item.description:
Jessie Ray – October 2026

Overview

This article details my journey in converting my Celestron CG5 mount to OnStep. I am not quite done tweaking it just yet, so this article may get updated in the future or I will write additional articles and link them here.

Included here will be:

  • The purchases I made
  • An explanation of the config
  • Some difficulties I had

The Reason

One may wonder why even bother doing an OnStep conversion. And honestly, I probably wouldn’t have even bothered, except that the electronics in my mount went haywire. It would often freak out, not knowing where it was, and then my scope would end up crashing into my tripod at night. The tracking was also completely off due to these errors. It would also just stop communicating between ASCOM and the hand controller. (Note that these old mounts do not have USB, so the best way to interface with them is via USB on the bottom of the HC).

item.title: Telescope Levelers
item.description:
(Ray O’Connor – 2024)

At the Natural Tunnel State Park where we do outreach, we make use of an older, park-owned telescope; a 10” Meade, Schmidt Cassegrain, model LX-50. We use the scope as you would any other and, knowing the sky as we do, never use its original intended functions. A keypad and small readout screen on a handset prompts the user which direction to slew the scope, guiding you to a known object (e.g. M13, or NGC 884). These older telescopes are known as “Push To” scopes, and are the predecessors to the standard “Go To” scopes, seen everywhere today.

item.title: Touring The Galaxy 2026
item.description: Touring the Galaxy is a recurring public outreach astronomy event held at the Natural Tunnel State Park. All are welcome whether you have a telescope or not. Park volunteers will take you on a journey through space using your own two eyes and a telescope. You will hear descriptions of many objects and constellations in the night sky and get the chance to see things you have never seen before!

item.title: New Site!
item.description:
Welcome to the new version of the Southwest Virginia Astronomy website!

Please bear with me as I update it and get content posted. This change was made due to the old version of the site being difficult to maintain and because a full Wordpress site is overkill for what this site is used for.

If you are new here, welcome! This is intended as a place where more technical and long form posts can be made since most people are not going to be interested in reading long form content on Facebook. I post full tutorials, articles, and observing logs here as well as any recurring local events I know about.
